identity.title: Regular rapid pounding in the neck / visible neck pulsations during episodes (frog sign)

technique.how: Ask whether, during episodes, the patient feels a rapid regular pounding or fluttering in the neck, and whether they or others have seen the neck veins pulsating rapidly (frog sign). If an episode is witnessed, look at the neck for rapid, regular jugular pulsations.
technique.prerequisites: Recurrent episodic palpitations that the patient can describe; direct observation only if an episode occurs in front of you.

interpretation.positive_finding: A regular rapid pounding sensation in the neck during palpitations makes AVNRT very likely (LR 177); visible neck pulsations raise it modestly (LR 2.7). Mechanism is atrial contraction against closed AV valves producing cannon A waves.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of the regular neck-pounding sensation makes AVNRT unlikely (LR 0.07) but says nothing about other arrhythmias such as AF, atrial flutter or VT.
interpretation.pitfalls: The estimate is for AVNRT specifically, not for 'any clinically significant arrhythmia', and derives from a single referral-centre study with very wide confidence intervals. Irregular neck pulsation suggests AF or ectopy rather than AVNRT.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: pursue SVT diagnosis (ECG during symptoms, event monitor, EP referral); negative: AVNRT unlikely, keep other arrhythmias on the differential.

estimates.target_condition: Atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia (AVNRT) in patients with palpitations (finding: regular rapid-pounding sensation in the neck, present)
estimates.population: Patients with palpitations/documented paroxysmal SVT undergoing reference-standard rhythm documentation (RCE pooled analysis; data from a single referral cohort)
estimates.reference_standard: Electrophysiologic study / ECG-documented arrhythmia mechanism (as summarized by the RCE)
estimates.quote: The presence of a regular rapid-pounding sensation in the neck (LR, 177; 95% CI, 25-1251)

estimates.target_condition: AVNRT in patients with palpitations (finding: regular rapid-pounding sensation in the neck, ABSENT)
estimates.reference_standard: Electrophysiologic study / ECG-documented arrhythmia mechanism (as summarized by the RCE)
estimates.quote: The absence of a regular rapid-pounding sensation in the neck makes detecting the same arrhythmia less likely (LR, 0.07; 95% CI, 0.03-0.19).

estimates.target_condition: AVNRT in patients with palpitations (finding: visible neck pulsations during palpitations)
estimates.reference_standard: Electrophysiologic study / ECG-documented arrhythmia mechanism (as summarized by the RCE)
estimates.quote: visible neck pulsations (LR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.25-5.78) in association with palpitations increases the likelihood of a specific type of arrhythmia

sources.citation: Thavendiranathan P, Bagai A, Khoo C, Dorian P, Choudhry NK. Does this patient with palpitations have a cardiac arrhythmia? JAMA. 2009;302(19):2135-2143.

Gursoy S, Steurer G, Brugada J, Andries E, Brugada P. Brief report: the hemodynamic mechanism of pounding in the neck in atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia. N Engl J Med. 1992;327(11):772-774.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative response to exclude clinically significant arrhythmia in general; the RCE concludes the clinical examination cannot exclude arrhythmia in most patients.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Neck pounding with syncope, chest pain or pre-excitation on ECG needs urgent ECG capture and cardiology/EP referral.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Patient-reported symptom; the very wide CI (25-1251) reflects a single small study. Sensitivity/specificity underlying the LRs are in the RCE table, which was not accessible.

extraction_notes: LRs are taken verbatim from the Thavendiranathan 2009 RCE abstract (not open access; Table with sens/spec not viewable, so sensitivity/specificity are left null rather than back-derived from the LR). The RCE abstract notes most accuracy data come from single small studies; evidence_level set to single_study accordingly. Target condition is AVNRT specifically, not any arrhythmia. Gursoy 1992 NEJM (PMID 1501653, confirmed by fetch; PubMed carries no abstract) is cited as the mechanistic/primary source for neck pounding in AVNRT; no number is taken from it because its text is not accessible. The absent-finding LR is entered as a separate estimate so each quote contains its own number.
